blocks.text: Cephalon Ordis, appointed keeper of the Arsenal. Every corner is in perfect order. Help yourself, Operator.

Your damage and your survival both ride on your cards, Tenno. Your weapon and your own body each have eight mod slots. <hl>Mods</hl> are upgrade cards you slot into weapons or Warframes, each carrying a few <t>stats</t> such as '+120% {lang:kuvaweapon.item_attribute_type.meleeDamage}'. Installing one doesn't use it up, and you can pull it out and move it elsewhere at any time.

In the Origin System, a Mod is an upgrade card slotted into a Warframe or a weapon; here the same thing is called a mod. Each piece of gear has room for only so many, so deciding which to keep and how to combine them is the heart of any build.
<dim>Kuva, Requiem, Riven and similar terms come from Warframe; look up any you don't know in [[start/glossary]].</dim>

rows: A consecrated weapon, <t>8</t> slots each; the mods travel with that weapon
When you attack with it in your main hand

blocks.title: What 'consecrated' means
blocks.text: <hl>Consecrating</hl> gives an item a weapon stat panel; an item without one takes no weapon mods. [[weapons/kuva_weapons|Kuva weapons]] come consecrated. For swords, bows, shields, armor and the like, put them in the {item:kuvalich:requiem_evolve} first and consecrate them with a {item:kuvalich:riven_sliver}; see [[weapons/requiem_evolve]].
Step 1: get mods

rows: When [[world/requiem_ore|Requiem Ore]] drops a Requiem card
An unrevealed Bronze / Silver / Gold mod
Finishing a [[enemies/kuva_master|Kuva Lich]] on a successful decryption
Always one unrevealed Prime or Riven mod
Merging three into one at the [[weapons/requiem_recast|Requiem Recast]]

blocks.text: <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.moduleWeaponRatio|pctv}</t> of dropped mods are weapon mods; the rest are Warframe mods.
Step 2: reveal

items: Spot an <t>unrevealed</t> card: its name says so, its stats read <dim>+??% ???</dim>, and it can't be installed yet.
Hold it in your <w>main hand</w> and right-click. The off-hand does nothing.
The card vanishes and a revealed mod drops at your feet. Pick it up.

blocks.text: Step 3: install

items: Put a consecrated weapon into the weapon slot of the {item:kuvalich:requiem_weapon_table}.
Drag mods into the 8 mod slots, or <t>Shift + click</t> one in your inventory to send it to a slot that accepts it.
Take the weapon out and the mods are written onto it. To swap, put it back and pull the card out; removing mods costs nothing.

blocks.text: Warframe mods are simpler: open the {item:kuvalich:requiem_warframe_table} and drop them straight into its slots; see [[warframe/warframe_module]].

blocks.title: Check the level first
blocks.text: A newly revealed mod is usually level <t>1</t> and gives only 1/{cfg:kuva_lich.moduleMaxLevel} of its full effect, so at first it seems to do little. Level it up first; see [[modules/module_level]].

blocks.title: When it won't fit
blocks.text: Usually it's one of three things: two copies of the same mod, more than 1 Riven mod, or a card that isn't revealed yet. Pick up a mod in an arsenal and watch for slots that pulse red; those are the conflicts. The full rules are in [[modules/module_limits]].

entries.title: Mod rules and limits
entries.summary: Slots, conflicts, one Riven and other rules

blocks.text: These rules decide which mods a weapon or Warframe can take. When an arsenal won't let you place a mod, go down the list, Tenno; the reason is in there.

items: Every weapon or Warframe has exactly <t>8</t> slots, whatever its level.
One copy of each mod. The normal, Prime and [[modules/module_rarity|Galvanized]] versions count as the same mod, so only one of Fury, Fury Prime and Galvanized Fury can go in.
Mods that boost the same stat may also conflict. True Steel and Lethal Combo both add melee critical chance, so only one of them fits.
At most <t>1</t> [[modules/riven_module|Riven mod]] per item.
Unrevealed cards can't be installed, so reveal them first with a main-hand right-click.

blocks.title: Watch for red
blocks.text: When you pick up a mod in an arsenal, the slots that conflict with it pulse red, and when a Shift + click fails, the conflicting slots flash a few times. If you see red, pick another mod.
Mods that never come out of reveals
These types are never produced when you reveal a card: {cfg:modules.disabledModuleTypes|list} (internal type names)

items: Every version of such a type is included, whether normal, Prime, Galvanized or Executioner.

items.text: <g>Mods you already own are unaffected</g>; they can still be installed, work and level up.
<g>Mods you already own are unaffected</g>; they can still be installed and work.
Weapon Rivens are among them. Unrevealed weapon Rivens can't be revealed, and cycling one you already have wastes the Kuva.
Warframe Rivens are among them. Unrevealed Warframe Rivens can't be revealed, and cycling one you already have wastes the Kuva.

blocks.text: Value range per card
Some stats have a minimum and maximum on a single card, written as 'stat:min:max': <t>{cfg:modules.attributeValueRanges|list}</t>

items: Values outside the range count as the boundary, and unlisted stats are unrestricted.

items.text: The range applies to the max-level value, before level scaling. With a max of 3 (300%), a max-level +400% card counts as +300%, and as +150% at half level.
With a max of 3 (300%), a +400% card counts as +300%.

items: The card itself still shows the original number. Hold <t>Ctrl</t> on the weapon panel for the source view, which shows each card's value after the range is applied.

blocks.text: Total cap per stat
When several cards add the same stat, their total is capped, written as 'stat:cap': <t>{cfg:modules.attributeTotalCaps|list}</t>

items: Only positive totals are capped; negative totals are untouched, and unlisted stats are unrestricted too.

items.text: The cap applies to values after level scaling.

items: [[combat/kill_stack|Kill stack]] bonuses are added after the cap, so they can go past it.

items.text: Caps are counted per item. The 8 mods on your main-hand weapon are capped together, and so are your 8 Warframe mods; items in extra slots such as the off-hand are capped on their own and then added at their rate, see [[modules/multi_slot]].
Caps are counted per item. The 8 mods on your main-hand weapon are capped together, and so are your 8 Warframe mods.

items: Warframe fire, electric, homologous and fall resistances, along with shield recharge delay, multiply rather than add, so this cap doesn't apply to them.
When a stat gets cut, holding Ctrl on the weapon panel shows an extra section with the values before and after the cut.

blocks.text: Stat names in the rules
Stat names in the rules

Values in the rules are decimals, so <t>1</t> means 100% and <t>-0.5</t> means −50%; fixed-value stats such as fixed health, shield and armor are plain points. Common stat names are listed below, and the rest are in [[reference]].

Card value multipliers
Card value multipliers

items: Multipliers are applied when a card is created, by revealing or Riven cycling, so the numbers on the card already include them.
Key stats are critical chance, critical damage, status chance, status duration and shield recharge rate and delay, including critical chance and status chance on dash attacks.
The kill stack versions of melee critical damage, status chance and shield recharge are key stats too; everything else is a general stat.
Riven mods use only the general multiplier for all their stats.

Bronze, Silver and Gold tiers exist over there as well. Clear tiers make for tidy books, Ordis finds. A Primed Mod is a stronger version of a normal one, shortened here to Prime, and Galvanized Mods build up their bonus with every kill.
The same mod can exist in several tiers, such as Silver 'Fury' and Prime 'Fury Prime'. Don't let the names fool you: they <w>count as the same mod</w> and can't be installed together.

entries.title: Mod levels and Endo
entries.summary: Level scaling, upgrade costs, Endo sources
items: kuvalich:endo

blocks.text: Mods have no levels. Every card works at full strength as soon as you get it, Tenno, with no upgrading needed.

How much a card is worth depends on how far you level it. Mods have levels, up to <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.moduleMaxLevel}</t>. A newly revealed mod is usually level 1, and you raise it one level at a time with <hl>{item:kuvalich:endo}</hl>, the material made for upgrading mods.
Actual effect = max-level value × current level ÷ {cfg:kuva_lich.moduleMaxLevel}
A level 1 mod gives only 1/{cfg:kuva_lich.moduleMaxLevel} of its full value, which is why a new mod seems to do nothing.
The numbers on a card are already scaled to its level. The progress bar is followed by <t>Lv.current/max</t> and disappears at max level.
Waste not: a rule after Ordis's own heart. The archives say Mods are ranked up with Endo, and that dissolving Mods a Tenno no longer needs returns some of it.
Upgrading at the Requiem Forge

items: Open the {item:kuvalich:requiem_evolve} and put one revealed, not-yet-maxed mod in the left slot, one at a time.
Put {item:kuvalich:endo} in the material slot. The card now shows <t>Upgrade cost: N Endo</t>.
If you have enough, the right slot shows the mod one level higher. <g>Endo is only spent when you take it</g>.
Each upgrade adds only 1 level; put the new card back in the left slot to keep going.

blocks.text: How much Endo it takes
Higher levels cost more and lower rarities cost less. The last Prime level alone takes <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.endoLastLevelCost}</t>. Spend your Endo on the cards you will actually use.
Where Endo comes from

cells: Killing a hostile monster with a consecrated weapon in your main hand

rows: Dismantling a mod at the [[weapons/requiem_recast|Requiem Recast]]
Depends on rarity and level, at most 64

blocks.text: Mastery: leveling is never wasted
Leveling work stays with you. Once you've leveled a mod to some level at the Requiem Forge, every mod of the same type and rarity you <t>reveal</t> later comes out at that level.
Mastery only applies at the moment you right-click to reveal, and only counts levels gained at the Requiem Forge. Mods that are already revealed never level themselves up.
Deep intel
Level n → n+1 = {cfg:kuva_lich.endoLastLevelCost} × (n ÷ {cfg:kuva_lich.moduleMaxLevel|add:-1}) ^ {cfg:kuva_lich.endoCostExponent} × rarity factor

Rarity factors: <c:CD7F32>Bronze</c> 25%, <c:C0C0C0>Silver</c> 50%, <c:FFD700>Gold</c> 75%, <c:55FFFF>Prime</c> and <c:FF55FF>Riven</c> 100%. The first part is rounded, then multiplied by the rarity factor and rounded up, minimum 1.

items.text: Endo from kills only counts hostile monsters; slimes, ghasts, phantoms and the like don't count.

items: Mining Experience Ore with Silk Touch gives no Endo.
Dismantling a mod gives Bronze 1, Silver 2, Gold 4, Prime or Riven 8, plus 1 per level above 1, at most 64. The card is used up.
Rivens give extra when dismantled, +1 per cycle so far, plus +2 / +4 / +8 / +16 at disposition 2-5.

items.text: Mastery is tracked per type and rarity, so cards of the same type in the same tier share one record, such as Fury Prime and Galvanized Fury. Weapon Rivens are tracked separately for melee, ranged and universal, while Warframe Rivens share one record.

items: Cycling a Riven <g>keeps its level</g>, so you can level it first and cycle later; see [[modules/riven_module]].

entries.title: Mod codex
entries.summary: Press Tab in an arsenal to browse all mods

blocks.text: Operator, there are hundreds of mods, and there is no need to memorize them. Each arsenal has a built-in codex, the '{lang:kuvalich.codex.title.weapon}' and the '{lang:kuvalich.codex.title.warframe}', where you can browse mods and see their full cards. Ordis keeps both in immaculate order!

items: Open the {item:kuvalich:requiem_weapon_table} or the {item:kuvalich:requiem_warframe_table}.
Press <t>Tab</t> to open the matching codex.
Press Tab again to return to the arsenal. Esc first clears the search box and returns on a second press.

blocks.text: What's in the codex

items: Mods are grouped into Bronze, Silver, Gold and Prime, and each group header shows that tier's discovered and total counts.
The badge at the top right shows <t>discovered / total</t> for the whole codex.
Hover a mod to see its full card.

items.text: Values in the codex are shown at max level.

items: The search box at the top matches the name or any text on the card, including stat names and numbers. It ignores case and treats the whole input as one keyword.
Scroll with the mouse wheel or drag the scrollbar on the right.

blocks.text: The codex doesn't list <c:FF55FF>Riven mods</c> because their stats are random. Ordis has little patience for the unpredictable. See [[modules/riven_module]] for how they roll.
What counts as discovered

items: Picking up a revealed mod, or having one in your inventory, marks it as discovered.
Your inventory is scanned when you join the game and every 5 seconds after that.
Mods installed on a weapon or Warframe are not scanned.
Different rarities of the same mod are recorded separately.
Undiscovered cells show no icon, only a few scrambled lines, but hovering still shows the stats.

blocks.text: Creative mode

rows: Put one in your inventory; if your inventory is full it is refused and the cell flashes red
Install it straight into the first free valid slot of the current weapon, or of your Warframe
Refused on a conflict, when no slot is free, or when the Weapon Arsenal holds no weapon

entries.title: Riven mods
items: kuvalich:item_riven_module
kuvalich:warframe_riven_module

blocks.text: <c:FF55FF>Riven mods</c> have fully random stats, 2-3 positive ones and possibly 1 negative one, and they mainly drop when you finish a [[enemies/kuva_master|Kuva Lich]] on a successful decryption. Every reroll costs Kuva that you never get back. Count yours before you start, Tenno; luck will not pay the bill.
There are weapon Rivens and Warframe Rivens, and both must be revealed with a main-hand right-click first. Each weapon or Warframe can hold only <t>1</t>.
The mode is locked in the moment you reveal the card and never changes. Warframe Rivens have no mode; their names start with Warframe.
{lang:kuvaweapon.item_type_riven_trend.tooltip} (●●●○○)
Disposition is shown as 1-5 filled dots. It's decided on reveal and <w>never changes, not even when cycling</w>. More dots mean stronger stats but pricier cycles.
How the numbers are rolled
Each stat = base value × layout factor × disposition factor × random roll
Random roll: 0.9-1.1 for positive stats, 0.8-1.2 for the negative one.

For example, a {lang:kuvaweapon.item_attribute_type.meleeDamage} stat on a disposition 3 card with 2 positive and 1 negative stats has a base of 165%, so at max level it comes to about 165% × 1.2 × 1.0 × 0.9-1.1 = <t>178%-218%</t>.
All of the above is then multiplied by the general stat multiplier, <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.moduleAttributeMultiplier|x}</t>; see [[modules/module_limits]].
Cycling: rerolling with Kuva

items: Put a revealed Riven in the left slot of the {item:kuvalich:requiem_evolve} and enough {item:kuvalich:kuva} in the material slot. Where to get Kuva: [[start/materials]].
A card with new stats appears on the right at once. <w>This is when you pay for this cycle</w>, and the original card's cycle count goes up by 1.
To keep the new stats, take the right-hand card; the original disappears.
To keep the old stats, take the original back out of the left slot or close the screen. The new card is discarded, and the Kuva already paid is not refunded.

blocks.title: Every preview costs Kuva
blocks.text: Each preview is paid for once. If you add Kuva to the material slot or take some out after a preview, and what's left can still pay, it previews again with the new amount and charges again. You pay once per reroll. Once a preview is up, leave the material slot alone unless you mean to roll again.
How much Kuva a cycle costs
Weapon Riven: min(cycles so far, 8) + 2 × disposition − 1　|　Warframe Riven: min(cycles so far, 8) + disposition²
Each cell runs from the cost of the first cycle to the cap. Every cycle costs 1 more, and the cost stops rising after 8 cycles.
The cycle count appears on the card as '{lang:kuvaweapon.item_type_riven_cycle.tooltip}', hidden at 0. While the Requiem Forge screen is open, the card shows <t>Cycle cost: N Kuva</t> directly.

Operator, Riven Mods in the Origin System must also be unveiled by completing a challenge, and cycling them costs <x>Kuva-- Kuva-- KU--</x> hm. Recalibrated: cycling costs Kuva there as well. Disposition varies from weapon to weapon; the higher it is, the stronger the Riven's stats.

blocks.title: Weapon Rivens can't be revealed
blocks.text: Kuva Liches can still drop unrevealed weapon Rivens, but right-clicking won't reveal them. Don't cycle the weapon Rivens you already have; the Kuva is taken and no new card comes out. Dismantle unwanted ones at the [[weapons/requiem_recast|Requiem Recast]].

blocks.title: Warframe Rivens can't be revealed
blocks.text: Kuva Liches can still drop unrevealed Warframe Rivens, but right-clicking won't reveal them. Don't cycle the Warframe Rivens you already have; the Kuva is taken and no new card comes out. Dismantle unwanted ones at the [[weapons/requiem_recast|Requiem Recast]].
Deep intel

items: Disposition odds on reveal: 5 dots 2.5%, 4 dots about 4.9%, 1-3 dots about 30.9% each.
Weapon Rivens never roll [[combat/elements|combined elements]], which are Gas, Radiation, Magnetic, Corrosive, Blast and Viral; combined elements mostly appear on Gold and Prime mods.
The negative stat is never a kill stack stat.

On weapon Rivens the negative stat is also never one of the four base elements, {lang:kuvaweapon.item_attribute_type.true_bullet}, {lang:kuvaweapon.item_attribute_type.gun_loot_drop}, {lang:kuvaweapon.item_attribute_type.execute_threshold}, {lang:kuvaweapon.item_attribute_type.purge_buff} or {lang:kuvaweapon.item_attribute_type.execute_chance}.

items.text: Gun-only stats, including multishot, fire rate and burst radius, can also appear on ranged and universal weapon Rivens.

items: Warframe Rivens never roll fixed-value stats such as fixed health, shield or armor.
A cycled card keeps the original's mode and disposition; its name is re-rolled.

items.text: Cycling keeps the level too, so you can level a Riven first and cycle later.

entries.title: Multi-slot bonuses
entries.summary: Mods on off-hand and other slots add bonuses

blocks.text: Mods on your main-hand weapon always work at full strength. Items in the slots listed below can also add their mod bonuses to your attacks at a reduced rate, as long as they are <hl>consecrated and modded</hl>. Beyond your main hand, these slots count toward your strength too, Tenno.
Extra bonus = mod bonuses on that item × the slot's effect rate × that item's panel damage multiplier
So put items with a high panel damage multiplier in these slots.

For example, an off-hand shield carries a max-level +100% {lang:kuvaweapon.item_attribute_type.meleeDamage}, its panel damage multiplier is 1.2 and the off-hand rate is {cfg:kuva_lich.offhandEffectMultiplier|pctv}, so you gain an extra <t>+{cfg:kuva_lich.offhandEffectMultiplier|mul:1.2|pctv}</t>.
How to use it

items: Consecrate the item in the {item:kuvalich:requiem_evolve} using a {item:kuvalich:riven_sliver}.
Put it in the {item:kuvalich:requiem_weapon_table} and install weapon mods on it as you would on a weapon.
Put it in one of the slots listed above.
Attack with a consecrated weapon in your main hand; the bonus is added then.

blocks.title: Both must be consecrated
blocks.text: 1) Items in these slots must be consecrated, or their mods don't count. 2) Your main hand must hold a consecrated weapon too. With an ordinary item in your main hand, the whole mod system stays out of damage calculation, extra bonuses included.
These bonuses are merged into your main-hand weapon's panel (see [[weapons/weapon_panel]]), and they don't use up any of its 8 slots.
<dim>Total caps are counted per item here: each item is capped on its own, separately from the main hand, see [[modules/module_limits]].</dim>
